items.informal_name: Degree Reduction via Leading Term Cancellation with Commuting Coefficients
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Ring R] {p q : Polynomial R},
  p.leadingCoeff * q.leadingCoeff = q.leadingCoeff * p.leadingCoeff →
    p.natDegree ≤ q.natDegree → 0 < q.natDegree → (p.cancelLeads q).natDegree < q.natDegree
items.informal_description: Let $ p $ and $ q $ be polynomials over a commutative ring with commuting leading coefficients. If $ \deg(p) \leq \deg(q) $ and $ q $ is non-constant (i.e., $ \deg(q) > 0 $), then the natural degree of the polynomial obtained by canceling the leading terms of $ p $ and $ q $ is strictly less than $ \deg(q) $.

items.informal_name: Strict Decrease of Polynomial Degree After Reduction Under Monomial Order
items.informal_description: Let $ f $ and $ b $ be multivariate polynomials over a commutative semiring $ R $ with variables indexed by $ \sigma $. Suppose the leading coefficient of $ b $ is invertible, $ \deg_m(b) \leq \deg_m(f) $ under the monomial order $ m $, and $ \deg_m(f) \neq 0 $. Then, the degree of the polynomial obtained by reducing $ f $ with respect to $ b $ satisfies $ \deg_m(\text{reduce}(f, b)) \prec_m \deg_m(f) $.

items.informal_name: Supremum Degree of Difference is Strictly Less When Leading Coefficients are Equal
items.type:
∀ {A : Type u_3} {B : Type u_5} [inst : LinearOrder B] [inst_1 : OrderBot B] {D : A → B} [inst_2 : AddZeroClass A],
  Function.Injective D →
    ∀ {R : Type u_8} [inst_3 : Ring R] {p q : AddMonoidAlgebra R A},
      AddMonoidAlgebra.supDegree D p = AddMonoidAlgebra.supDegree D q →
        AddMonoidAlgebra.leadingCoeff D p = AddMonoidAlgebra.leadingCoeff D q →
          AddMonoidAlgebra.supDegree D (p - q) < AddMonoidAlgebra.supDegree D p ∨ p = q
items.informal_description: Let $ D $ be an injective degree function on an additive monoid $ A $, and let $ R $ be a ring. For elements $ p, q $ in the additive monoid algebra $ R[A] $, if $ \sup\{D(a) \mid a \in \text{supp}(p)\} = \sup\{D(a) \mid a \in \text{supp}(q)\} $ and the leading coefficients of $ p $ and $ q $ are equal, then $ \sup\{D(a) \mid a \in \text{supp}(p - q)\} < \sup\{D(a) \mid a \in \text{supp}(p)\} $ or $ p = q $.

items.informal_description: Let $ s $ be a finite set of elements of type $ \iota $, and let $ f : \iota \to \kappa $ be a function into an additive commutative monoid $ \kappa $ equipped with a strict total order $ <$ and strict left-monotonicity of addition. If $ d \in s $ and $ 0 < f(d) $, then the sum of $ f $ over $ s \setminus \{d\} $ is strictly less than the sum of $ f $ over $ s $, i.e., $ \sum_{m \in s \setminus \{d\}} f(m) < \sum_{m \in s} f(m) $.

items.informal_name: Strict Sum Inequality for Lists in an Ordered Additive Monoid
items.type:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {M : Type u_3} [inst : AddMonoid M] [inst_1 : Preorder M] [AddLeftStrictMono M] [AddLeftMono M]
  [AddRightStrictMono M] [AddRightMono M] {l : List ι} (f g : ι → M),
  (∀ (i : ι), i ∈ l → f i ≤ g i) → (∃ i, i ∈ l ∧ f i < g i) → (List.map f l).sum < (List.map g l).sum
items.informal_description: Let $ M $ be an additive monoid equipped with a preorder where addition is both left and right monotonic (strictly and non-strictly). For any list $ l $ of elements in an index set $ \iota $, and functions $ f, g : \iota \to M $ such that $ f(i) \leq g(i) $ for all $ i \in l $ and $ f(i) < g(i) $ for some $ i \in l $, it holds that $ \sum_{i \in l} f(i) < \sum_{i \in l} g(i) $.

items.informal_name: Strict Monotonicity of Finite Sum in Ordered Cancellative Additive Monoids
items.type:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {M : Type u_4} [inst : Fintype ι] [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M] [inst_2 : PartialOrder M]
  [IsOrderedCancelAddMonoid M], StrictMono fun f => ∑ x, f x
items.informal_description: For a finite type $\iota$ and an ordered cancellative additive monoid $M$, the function mapping each function $f : \iota \to M$ to the sum $\sum_{x \in \iota} f(x)$ is strictly monotonic. This means that if $f(x) < g(x)$ for all $x \in \iota$, then $\sum_{x \in \iota} f(x) < \sum_{x \in \iota} g(x)$.
